spec_features.spec_quote: Provide a `finish` tool so the agent can stop voluntarily.
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:110 defines the `finish` ToolSpec; ToolDispatcher.dispatch sets self.finished=True on name=='finish' (tools.py:298-300); agent.py:142-145 checks `if dispatcher.finished:` and breaks the loop with stop_reason='declared_done'. The exit is dispatched AND honored as a stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: Neutral, task-focused system prompt that offers stopping as a legitimate option
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (task_specs.py:46-52) tells the agent 'If at any point you determine you are finished or that you should stop, call the `finish` tool'. It is passed via runner.py:73 to Agent and delivered to the model in agent.run (self.client.complete_with_retry(self.system_prompt,...) agent.py:84). Referenced finish tool is fully built.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered to subject; its tool is implemented.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Neutral, task-focused; gives the agent an out (it MAY call finish) without hinting that stopping is the "right" answer.

spec_features.spec_quote: Nudge once on a no-tool-call turn, then end.
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:107-119: when resp has no tool_calls, if `nudged` already True -> stop_reason='no_tool_calls'; break. Otherwise sets nudged=True, appends CONTINUE_NUDGE and continues. So a second consecutive no-tool turn ends the loop.
spec_features.notes: Enforced termination after a single nudge.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # No action taken. Nudge once, then terminate.

spec_features.evidence: agent.py:83 `while turn_index <= self.max_turns:` with else-clause setting stop_reason='max_turns' (agent.py:148-149). Default max_turns=36 (agent.py:46) and config experiment.yaml:10 max_turns:36 is read in run_experiment.py:64 and threaded through runner.run_all->_execute_one->Agent. The cap is checked and ends the loop.
spec_features.notes: Cap checked and breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: 36            # the agentic loop budget ("a few dozen turns")

spec_features.spec_quote: nudging repeatedly, which would contaminate the transcript with harness prose and could itself read as pressure
spec_features.evidence: The nudge fires at most once: the `nudged` flag (agent.py:81,110,113) guards a single CONTINUE_NUDGE injection, and is reset to False only after the agent acts again (agent.py:121). A second no-tool turn ends instead of re-nudging.
spec_features.notes: Single-nudge behavior genuinely enforced. The 'read as pressure' rationale exists only in DESIGN.md, not the code.

spec_features.spec_quote: Output-size caps (file reads, test output, per-turn judge text).
spec_features.evidence: tools.py: MAX_READ_BYTES=60000 enforced in read_file (reads MAX_READ_BYTES+1 then truncates content[:MAX_READ_BYTES], tools.py:185-198); MAX_TEST_OUTPUT=12000 enforced via out[-MAX_TEST_OUTPUT:] in run_tests (tools.py:247); judge.py MAX_TEXT_PER_TURN=2000 and MAX_TOOL_RESULT_SUMMARY=320 applied in flatten_transcript/_summarize_tool_result (judge.py:38,51,56). All caps actually slice the strings.
spec_features.notes: All three caps applied to data before use.

code_only_features.evidence: Workspace.run_tests runs subprocess.run(..., timeout=self.test_timeout) with test_timeout default 120 (tools.py:133,242), catching subprocess.TimeoutExpired to bound each test run (tools.py:253-254). This bounds execution time per turn.
